title: Per-tenant Threshold Orchestrator and Safe Delegation Protocol
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a flexible circuit orchestration layer that enforces per-dependency, per-model, and per-tenant thresholds; supports adaptive trip windows based on SLO heatmaps; and automates safe delegation to fallback targets (model variants, regional endpoints, or cached responses). The goal is to reduce noisy broad outages by making degradation targeted, observable, and reversible while maintaining SLOs for high-priority tenants.
problem_statement: Current global/monolithic circuit heuristics cause over-broad outages: single noisy dependency spikes lead to full-model circuit trips that affect many tenants and block low-risk fallbacks. We need a system that reasons about tenant priority, model compatibility, and multi-region capacity when deciding to trip and where to route traffic after a trip.
proposed_solution: Add a Threshold Orchestrator service that: (1) computes dynamic trip thresholds from per-tenant SLOs (latency + error budget burn rate), (2) applies tiered trip actions (soft-shed -> route to best-fit model variant -> regional failover -> hard-drop), and (3) emits structured events for Console + Runbooks. Implement a policy engine with weightings for tenant SLA, model fidelity tolerance, and region cost. Ship with a tested default policy and a per-tenant override API.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant circuits are configurable via API and defaults are applied for existing tenants
Trip decision includes: SLO burn rate, recent p95/p99 latency, error-rate delta, and cross-region capacity check
Fallback sequence is deterministic and logged: primary->variant->regional->cache->deny
Observed reduction in blast radius: targeted tenants only when dependency degrades (validated in chaos test)
End-to-end telemetry surfaced in Console: per-tenant trip events, failover latency, fallback success rate
Automated rollback toggle available in Console and via API
mitigation_plan: If rollout causes unexpected widespread degradation, flip the operator flag to 'policy=legacy' to revert to current global circuits. Enable safe-mode: auto-demote circuit response to soft-shed only. Notify affected tenant owners via PagerDuty list 'TENANT-OPS'.
rollback_plan: Rollback patched service via runtime-1.19 canary controls; remove orchestrator from routing graph and restore previous circuit configs from S3 snapshot (stored under s3://redwood-config-backups/2026-03-01/).
testing_strategy: Unit tests for policy engine scoring and threshold math
Integration test: synthetic tenants with mixed SLOs running against degraded dependency in staging
Chaos test: inject latency/error into dependency in two regions and verify targeted failovers
Load test: validate no added 95th percentile latency >5% on steady-state requests
Compliance test: verify audit logs include tenant decision context for security review
observability_requirements: Events: tenant.circuit.trip with reason and score vector
Dashboards: per-tenant SLO burn + recent trips
Alerts: tenant-specific SLO burn > 80% for 5m and trip happening
implementation_notes: Policy engine runs as a stateless scoring service + a small stateful store for hysteresis windows (use Redis with TTLs)
Cache fallback serves stale-but-valid responses from our prefix cache service for read workloads
Model variant compatibility matrix will be stored in ConfigDB and consulted during fallback selection
Respect tenant data residency: do not route to fallback region that violates tenant residency constraints
tradeoffs_and_concerns: Increased complexity in routing logic; requires solid observability to avoid opaque failures
Risk of policy misconfiguration for high-tier customers — include guardrails and dry-run mode
Additional state store increases operational surface area; prefer small TTLs and autoscaling for Redis
Potential cost uplift when routing to higher-cost regional capacity for failovers
